text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly implements national-scale spatial modeling of future agricultural land use across the entire Netherlands using a 500×500 m grid. Its primary objective is to simulate and compare alternative LULC futures under two socio-economic scenarios ("Global Economy" and "Regional Community"). It uses the Land Use Scanner model to produce mapped projections of agricultural and other land uses to 2030, with quantitative scenario-based comparisons of land area changes (e.g., Figure 1 and Table 1). The outputs include spatially explicit maps (Figure 2) and quantitative estimates of land conversion. All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with mapped outputs, and even though specific accuracy metrics like kappa or overall accuracy are not reported, the model incorporates quantitative suitability functions and calibrated demand estimates from sectoral models, satisfying the requirement for quantitative spatial modeling. None of the exclusion criteria apply.)
